title: Soft Body Simulation Improvement | Clo 2025.1 Features Deep Dive
description:
The new update to our hardware in CLO 2025.1 allows you to apply soft body simulation not only to CLO avatars but also to non-rigged custom avatars for more realistic deformation and movement.

Check out other new features here:https://clo3d.com/en/clo/features

Questions? Comment below or ask in our CLO discord server: https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/7814962429977-How-can-I-join-CLO-Discord?utm_campaign=multi_item_banner_JointheOfficialCLODiscord&utm_medium=referral&utm_source=later-linkinbio

summary: # Soft Body Simulation Improvement | Clo 2025.1 Features Deep Dive ## Introduction Hey everyone, it's Phoebe here, and I have some great updates to share with you on our Softbody feature. So let's dive on in and have some fun while we learn! ## Enabling Softbody Simulation Okay, so here I have my 3D window open. I’m first just going to walk you through how you can turn on Softbody and the latest updates. Originally, you could always turn on Softbody as long as the avatar was rigged, meaning it has a skeleton. But now, what we've done is allow you to add Softbody to avatars even if they aren't rigged or don’t have a skeleton. ### Selecting the Avatar Here I have an avatar. I'm just going to hide my patterns. This avatar is not rigged at all. I can go over to my toggle menu, select my avatar, and then choose "Show Avatar Joints." As you can see, there really aren't any joints. I’ll hide that again. ### Turning on Softbody Now, I can simply select this avatar or OBJ and go into my property editor to turn on Softbody simulation. Now that I have this on, I can play around with this slider to adjust the softness; I can make it really plushy or increase it so it's really stiff. The higher I go, the stiffer it is, and the lower I go, the less stiff it becomes. I’m going to have it set pretty low. ### Simulating the Softbody Now I’m just going to hit simulate, and you’ll see in real-time how this starts to bounce and conform, getting squishy and all of that. I’ll show you how this works. ## Displaying Patterns To show my pattern pieces, I’m going to hit Shift + W, which is the shortcut. I could also go into my toggle menu in the garment display and select "Show Garment." ### Interacting with Patterns What I can do here is click on my pattern pieces, and you'll see them start to move. For example, I can push this in, and you’ll start to see the avatar deforming and getting pushed in. If I hide this, you can see the movement, which is really cool. ### Adjusting Stiffness If I select this avatar and change the stiffness, you’ll see in real-time how it changes. As I increase the stiffness, the avatar gets stiffer; when I lower it, you can see it dropping a little bit and then rising again. ## Practical Applications Now that we understand how it works, let’s jump into how you could practically use it. Here I have my garment, and I’m going to bring in some shoulder pads. I also think this could be great for bras and backpacks. I’ll show you the shoulder pad example because I created that OBJ, and it works well. ### Importing the OBJ I’m going to go to File > Import > Add OBJ. One thing to know is if you're going to import your OBJ, just make sure that it is a clean OBJ—there are no intersections and no holes. If there are holes or intersections, then it will not work, and the Softbody simulation won’t be possible. ### Positioning the Shoulder Pads Here, I’m just going to select this and first make these a little bit smaller because they are a bit too big. Then, I’ll move this over and start to place them where I want them to be. ### Simulating the Shoulder Pads Now, before I even turn on any Softbody, I’m just going to simulate and let my garment sit on this new OBJ to get everything set up. Cool! Now, I’m going to hide the garment, select the shoulder pads, and turn on Softbody. I’m going to keep this at 800 and simulate. As you can see, it’s already simulated in there. If I select this and lower the stiffness, I can simulate again. The garment isn’t really putting much pressure on this, so you won’t see the foam compress much. But if I actively put pressure on it, you’ll start to see it go down and spring back up. ### Using Avatar Tape Another cool feature you can use is the avatar tape. I could turn on some avatar tape here, attach it, and then simulate. You’ll actually see it move and attach straight to that, which is really cool. Just a note: the tacking won’t work, but the avatar tape does. You can see how this is attached. ## Mesh Issues and Troubleshooting Before we finish up, I just want to show you quickly what will happen if I try to bring in an OBJ that has some mesh issues. If I go and import an OBJ, this last one, and select it, then turn on Softbody and hit simulate, a warning will come up. ### Identifying Mesh Problems All of these warnings will also appear, telling you that there is an open hole issue and a self-intersection. I can hit "OK," and then go into my toggle menu again to hit "Show Wireframe." I’ll see where these issues are—like here, and here, there are holes and all of that. ### Fixing Mesh Issues I would just have to go into my 3D modeling software and fix that mesh so that I could bring it in and apply a proper Softbody simulation to it. ## Conclusion Thank you so much for watching! If you have any questions, use the comment section down below. Don’t forget to like and subscribe, and keep having fun in the cloud. Thanks again!
